title: Kahana vs Goodreads: Shared Reading, Not a Private Progress Bar
excerpt: Goodreads is book tracking, ratings, reviews, and social reading lists, where many readers already log what they read. Kahana is clubs and hubs around the books you actually read together.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: 125M+ members and 3.5B books listed in the database.
Deep Amazon integration: purchase paths to Amazon and Kindle sync for quotes, notes, and reading progress.

strengths.title: Discovery and recommendations
strengths.detail: Large catalog with aggregated ratings and reviews helps readers find books they will like.

strengths.title: Social reading features
strengths.detail: Shelves, reading progress, quotes, and discussions; follow friends and authors.

strengths.title: Author tools
strengths.detail: Authors can claim profiles, link books, and interact with fans via Q&A and updates.

strengths.title: Kindle / Amazon integration
strengths.detail: Reading activity can sync from Kindle; short path from discovery to purchase.

weaknesses.title: Dated UI/UX
weaknesses.detail: Interface is often called clunky and old-fashioned; navigation can feel unwieldy.

weaknesses.title: Review quality and moderation
weaknesses.detail: Mixed review quality; complaints about troll ratings, spam shelves, and limited moderation tools.

weaknesses.title: Limited social depth
weaknesses.detail: Social features exist but clubs and discussion feel basic vs dedicated community platforms.

weaknesses.title: Ownership and data lock-in
weaknesses.detail: Amazon-owned; some users are uneasy about data and platform control.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Goodreads is book tracking, ratings, reviews, and social reading lists, where many readers already log what they read. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Goodreads is the world's largest site for readers and book recommendations.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Goodreads side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Goodreads you can use Ebook as a first-class product job. You need a dedicated reader, a giant store, or social tracking of everything you have ever read.

Using Kahana with Goodreads

You can use both. Goodreads keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep the reader or tracker you already use. Put the Club pick, discussion questions, and related files on Kahana so the book is a shared library item, not only a private progress bar.
